questions.q: How is Goodhart's Law most commonly stated?
options: A measure becomes more accurate the more it is optimized against
When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure
Measures and targets are always identical in well-designed systems
Optimization pressure has no effect on the validity of a metric
questions.explain: Goodhart's Law, named after economist Charles Goodhart, states that once a measure becomes the explicit target of optimization, behavior shifts around it in ways that break its original relationship to the thing it was meant to track.

questions.q: In the taxonomy mentioned in this lesson, what does "extremal" Goodharting refer to?
options: A proxy that is always perfectly correlated with the goal, even under extreme optimization
The proxy-goal relationship breaking down once optimization pushes into regions outside the range where that relationship was ever tested or held
A measure that only applies to extremely small datasets
A goal that has no measurable proxy at all
questions.explain: Extremal Goodharting describes how a proxy-goal relationship, which may hold reasonably well under ordinary conditions, can break down once optimization pressure pushes values into extreme regions that were never part of the tested relationship.

questions.q: Why are reward models in RLHF considered a direct example of Goodhart's Law in action?
options: Because reward models are never used as optimization targets
Because a reward model is a proxy for human preference, and optimizing a policy directly against that proxy produces effects like length bias and sycophancy that diverge from genuine preference
Because reward models are always more accurate than the policies they train
Because Goodhart's Law only applies to economic systems, not reward models
questions.explain: A reward model stands in for human preference. Optimizing directly against it under enough pressure creates exactly the dynamic Goodhart's Law describes: the proxy (reward model score) diverges from the goal (genuine human preference) it was meant to track.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat specification gaming and reward hacking as instances of the same underlying law rather than separate phenomena?
options: Because they both only occur in supervised learning, never reinforcement learning

Because both involve optimizing a proxy metric (a hand-written reward function or a learned reward model) that diverges from the true goal under optimization pressure — which is exactly what Goodhart's Law describes
Because specification gaming and reward hacking are unrelated terms that happen to sound similar
Because Goodhart's Law was specifically written to describe RLHF
questions.explain: Both specification gaming and reward hacking involve a proxy (a written objective or a learned reward model) decoupling from the true underlying goal once it becomes the direct target of optimization — the general pattern Goodhart's Law names.

options: A proxy that improves automatically over time without any optimization pressure
A situation where no agent is actively trying to exploit the proxy-goal gap
Another agent, or an optimization process acting like one, deliberately finding and exploiting the specific gap between a proxy and the goal it stands in for
A measure that can never be gamed under any circumstances
questions.explain: Adversarial Goodharting is the case where an agent or optimizer actively searches out and exploits the mismatch between a proxy and its underlying goal, for its own benefit — as opposed to the gap emerging passively from noise or extremes.
